Collocated Computations

1. What is Collocated Compute?
  • Collocated compute sends the computation to the node that owns a specific key;
  • The computation runs locally on that node, accessing data without any network hops;
  • This is one of Ignite's most powerful features — "send computation to data" instead of "send data to computation";
2. affinityRun / affinityCall
  • // Run a closure on the node that owns key=42 in "PersonCache"
ignite.compute().affinityRun("PersonCache", 42, () -> {
    IgniteCache<Integer, Person> cache = Ignition.localIgnite().cache("PersonCache");
    Person person = cache.localPeek(42); // local read — no network
    System.out.println("Name: " + person.getName());
});

// affinityCall returns a value
String name = ignite.compute().affinityCall("PersonCache", 42, () -> {
    IgniteCache<Integer, Person> cache = Ignition.localIgnite().cache("PersonCache");
    Person person = cache.localPeek(42);
    return person.getName();
});
3. Why is this efficient?
  • Without collocated compute: 
    Application → (network) → Node holding data → (network) → Application
2 network hops + data serialization
  • With collocated compute: 
    Application → (network) → Node holding data (compute runs locally) → (network) → result
Only the small result is sent back; data stays on the node
  • For operations that read/write large objects but return small results, this is dramatically faster;
4. Multi-Cache Collocated Compute
  • If multiple caches are colocated (same affinity key), you can access all of them locally: 
    ignite.compute().affinityRun(
    Arrays.asList("CustomerCache", "OrderCache"), // multiple caches
    customerId,                                    // affinity key
    () -> {
        Ignite local = Ignition.localIgnite();
        Customer c = local.cache("CustomerCache").localPeek(customerId);
        // Access all orders for this customer — all local!
    }
);
5. Use Cases
  • Aggregations — compute totals, averages, or summaries per partition locally;
  • Complex business logic — execute multi-step operations that involve reading and writing multiple related keys;
  • Data enrichment — join data from colocated caches and compute derived fields;
